content.thinking:
I'm going through the claims one by one. The first is that shoppers on io-shop had their account pages fail for a stated duration; I'm not checking the exact figure, just whether the general claim is supported, which it is by the Gbf7d source and the title. I'm also wondering whether "shoppers" means some or all, since the wording is generic. Next I'm moving on to the claim about IO Payments Ltd refusing payments, which I'm checking against T9 and Gbf7d.

I'm checking the rest of the claims: the lookup refusals and the peak error rate both hold up, and the customer loss estimate is supported. Nobody was paged, so no on-call responders were called in. Argus didn't act on the suspected cause because io-pay sits with IO Payments Ltd, which Argus can't reach, and its recommended step is to ask them to restore it rather than look for a code fix. That step hasn't been taken, and AI-1 is still open.

content.text: I checked all eight claims in the overview against the record and found none to flag. Each one matches the record's lines, mostly the error log row Gbf7d, the service register read T9 and the refusal at T16. The figures in braces weren't judged, as the instructions say.

supported.quote: For {duration}, shoppers on io-shop had their account pages fail.
IO Payments Ltd, the outside company that handles the shop's payments, began refusing the shop's requests to look up shoppers' saved cards.

At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing.

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, so no on-call responders were called in.

Its recommended step is to ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and it did not look for a code fix.
That step has not been taken.
